messages:
erin: quick follow-up on the shard-pool idea i posted yesterday — want to nail operator boundaries before we freeze the API

devon: skimmed. main concern: how do we guarantee the fast path latency without starving steady tenants?

erin: idea is a dual-lane model inside each pool: fast-path (prewarmed, low-packing) and steady-path (denser packing, tolerant of cold-starts)

kai: how do promotions/demotions happen? potential for thrash if we flip too quickly
erin: admission smoothing: require sustained demand. promotion triggers when fast_path_util > 0.8 for sustain_window_s (configurable). we move a small chunk (config: min_percent & max_absolute) and apply a cooldown
tessa: define the chunk size please. e.g. min(8% of pool, 1 gpu) or something predictable
erin: default: min(10% , 2 gpus). tenants with SLAs can request override up to contract limits
devon: billing: who bears extra cost when GPUs are carved to fast-path? need ledger semantics
erin: two-layer accounting: baseline reservation stays on tenant ledger; transient fast-path use goes to a burst ledger. ledger rows: tenant, amount_gpus, start_ts, end_ts, preemptible_flag
kai: eviction order? we must never evict pinned or gold SLA tenants in favor of bursts
erin: eviction priority (high->low): pinned_reservations, SLA=gold, SLA=silver, shared_burst_credit_holders, preemptible_low_priority
tessa: fairness across time — frequent small bursters could monopolize burst pool
erin: introduce burst_score with exponential decay (half-life ~1h). admission reduces priority for high recent share
devon: controller topology — single global reconciler vs operator-per-shard? implications for consistency and failover
erin: operator-per-shard + a lightweight global reconciler. local operator manages shard heuristics; global reconciler enforces pool-wide caps and cross-shard moves via leader-election
kai: can we see the config draft so I can validate logic against controller code?
erin: pasted snippet below:

```
pool_policy:
  fast_path:
    enabled: true
    min_gpus_percent: 0.05
    max_gpus_absolute: 4
    sustain_window_s: 60
    demotion_idle_s: 300
  cost_control:
    burst_ledger_enabled: true
    per_tenant_cap_tokens: 1000
    cap_refill_rate_per_min: 10
```

(we renamed promotion_window_s -> sustain_window_s after tessa's suggestion)

tessa: rollout plan? prefer region-by-region feature flag. also what metrics to watch?
erin: canary in us-west-2, 10% pools, 48h. metrics: fast_path_util, p99_latency_by_SLA, promotion_count, eviction_events, burst_ledger_debits
devon: KV cache worry: promoting an in-use instance might lose cached KV and spike latency
kai: prefer allocating idle instances into fast-path first. live-migrate/demote only when instance low-util and KV is sync-capable
erin: agreed — operator will prioritize cold allocations then graceful drain of steady nodes when necessary
orch-bot: deploy-planner: creating canary rollout checklist and preflight probes for us-west-2 pools
tessa: UX question: who owns tenant override UI? infra or product?
erin: infra exposes API; product builds console. field: fast_path_override_pct per tenant with contract-governed max
devon: retention for burst ledger? need long enough for billing disputes
erin: default 180d retention; after 30d compress to daily aggregates for storage savings
kai: test matrix: unit tests for admission math, k8s-integration for operator behavior, chaos for leader failover and promotion under churn
erin: i'll author the follow-up RFC tonight with schema + rollout checklist + dashboard wireframe
tessa: tiny nit: rename min_gpus_percent -> min_gpus_fraction? makes semantics clearer
erin: done in draft. thanks.
devon: ok sync tomorrow 10am PT to finalize rollout thresholds
erin: calendar invite sent. thanks all :thumbsup:
